parts.text:
One female observer noted features of every rider (passenger) standing or seated in the
critical area.
Identify two features she noted about every rider (passenger) in the critical area.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State one reason why the experiment was conducted between the two stations used.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Outline one conclusion from this study.

text: From the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the instructions given to the ‘teacher’ about how to deliver the shocks to the ‘learner’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify two examples of signs of ‘tension’ that were shown by the ‘teachers’ during the study.

text: From the study by Milgram (obedience):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why this study is from the learning approach.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one problem when using children in psychological research, using this study as an
example.

text: From the study by Saavedra and Silverman (button phobia):
Describe how the target words and foils were developed for the revised ‘Reading the Mind in the
Eyes’ test in the study by Baron-Cohen et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Identify two behaviours from participants in the euphoria condition that would be coded as
‘joins in activity’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one methodological strength of this study.

text: From the study by Schachter and Singer (two factors in emotion):
Describe the psychology being investigated in the study by Bandura et al. (aggression).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline the rating scale used in the Food History Inventory.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Outline one result from Experiment 1, using data collected from the Food History Inventory.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Suggest one real life application of this study.

text: From the study by Laney et al. (false memory):
Two friends, Kim and Alphonse, are discussing the ethics of the study by Pepperberg (parrot
learning). Kim thinks the study is ethical but Alphonse thinks it is unethical.
Explain one reason why Kim is correct and one reason why Alphonse is correct, using evidence
from this study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the two tasks the chimpanzees had to solve in the study by Yamamoto et al.
(chimpanzee helping).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one similarity and one difference between the study by Yamamoto et al. (chimpanzee
helping) and the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans).
